runs.market_commentary:
Asian markets surged dramatically overnight, with the Nikkei 225 closing up 2.12% at 66,399 and South Korea's KOSPI rallying a remarkable 4.61%, as regional investors responded positively to yen weakness and strong AI semiconductor demand signals. Mainland China's CSI 300 added 0.59%, supported by incremental domestic stimulus hopes. The standout performer in Asia underscores a sharp divergence from Western markets, where geopolitical anxiety is the dominant narrative.

European markets opened the week on the back foot, with Germany's DAX slipping 0.38% to 21,764 and the FTSE 100 fractionally lower at 8,702 (-0.18%), as energy-intensive industrials and consumer discretionary names feel the heat from surging oil prices. WTI crude jumped 0.92% to $92.32/bbl and Brent reached $97.13/bbl after renewed US-Iran war escalation over the Labor Day weekend stoked fears of prolonged supply disruption. The US dollar index strengthened 0.27% to 99.09 as safe-haven flows dominated early global trade.

US markets are closed today for Labor Day, making this a critical setup day for the four-day trading week ahead. Markets return Tuesday facing two binary macro events: the ECB rate decision Thursday (expected +25bp to 2.75%) and the August CPI print Friday. Last week's strong jobs report has already pushed Fed rate hike odds to 57% for September — a hot CPI reading above 3% Friday could cement that call and trigger a broad risk-asset repricing. Consumer sentiment fell to 51.7 in August from 55.2 in July, signaling elevated consumer anxiety that will sharpen the stakes on the Friday inflation print.

ideas.catalyst: WTI crude surged to $92.32/bbl (+0.92%) and Brent hit $97.13 as US-Iran war tensions escalated over Labor Day weekend, creating an immediate earnings tailwind for integrated oil majors.
ideas.thesis: Exxon's upstream operations generate exponentially higher free cash flow at $90+ oil versus the mid-$70s level that prevailed last week, with significant operating leverage at current prices. The US-Iran conflict trajectory points to sustained elevated prices through Q3 and into Q4, supporting multiple earnings beats and potential dividend acceleration or buyback acceleration beyond current guidance.
ideas.key_risk: A ceasefire or diplomatic breakthrough in US-Iran tensions could cause a rapid oil price reversal; watch for SPR releases or coordinated OPEC+ supply response as geopolitical risk premium unwinds.

ideas.catalyst: Active US-Iran war engagement and Middle East conflict escalation over Labor Day weekend creates a clear catalyst for accelerated defense procurement and potential emergency supplemental spending.
ideas.thesis: Lockheed Martin, as the premier US defense prime contractor, is positioned to benefit directly from increased US military spending tied to the ongoing US-Iran conflict, particularly demand for F-35 jets, THAAD missile defense systems, and precision munitions. Historical precedent from prior Middle East conflicts shows defense stocks re-rate higher and sustain premiums for 4-8 week periods following active conflict escalation phases.
ideas.key_risk: Any diplomatic de-escalation or Congressional pushback on emergency defense appropriations could cap the move; geopolitical risk is inherently unpredictable and peace can arrive quickly.

ideas.catalyst: Nikkei 225 closed +2.12% at 66,399 today while KOSPI surged 4.61% — Asian equity momentum is accelerating on yen weakness and AI semiconductor demand, with the Nikkei near multi-decade highs.
ideas.thesis: Japanese equities are benefiting from a combination of structural yen weakness (boosting exporter earnings), domestic AI investment themes, and central bank policy divergence as the BOJ remains more dovish than the hawkish Fed. EWJ provides liquid, diversified exposure to this secular trend while carrying lower concentration risk than individual Japanese ADRs.
ideas.key_risk: A surprise BOJ rate hike or sharp yen strengthening on safe-haven flows could rapidly reverse exporter gains; a risk-off global move from hot US CPI Friday would also spill into Asian markets.

ideas.catalyst: Markets now price a 57% probability of a September Fed rate hike; Friday's CPI could cement the hike and send long-duration yields sharply higher, crushing TLT.
ideas.thesis: The combination of a strong labor market, oil-driven inflationary pressure from the US-Iran conflict, and declining consumer sentiment creates a stagflationary backdrop that is toxic for long-duration Treasuries. A short TLT position profits from rising 10-year yields and provides a hedge against the dominant macro risk this week — a hot CPI print — while the dollar's strength confirms the hawkish repricing thesis.
ideas.key_risk: A surprise CPI miss below 2.5% would rapidly reprice the Fed dovish, causing a sharp TLT rally; US-Iran escalation could also trigger flight-to-safety Treasury buying that temporarily overwhelms the rate-hike narrative.

ideas.catalyst: FDA PDUFA date for zidesamtinib (ROS1+ non-small cell lung cancer) is September 18, 2026 — 11 days away — with management pre-positioning for commercial launch.
ideas.thesis: Zidesamtinib addresses a validated high-unmet-need oncology niche with strong clinical data in ROS1-positive NSCLC; ROS1 inhibitors have shown durable responses and FDA has been historically receptive to this well-characterized target. A positive September 18 decision would be transformative for this small-cap biotech, likely triggering institutional accumulation ahead of and immediately following approval.
ideas.key_risk: Binary FDA event — a Complete Response Letter or label restriction would send the stock sharply lower; position sizing must reflect the binary nature of the catalyst and the 11-day timeline.

ideas.catalyst: Morgan Stanley maintains NVDA as its core AI play; KOSPI's 4.61% surge today driven by HBM memory producers validates continued AI chip demand cycle through the back half of 2026.
ideas.thesis: NVIDIA's data center GPU franchise has no near-term competitive alternative at scale; the KOSPI surge reflects strength in SK Hynix and Samsung — HBM suppliers to NVIDIA's Blackwell and next-gen platforms — confirming robust end-demand across the entire semiconductor supply chain. AI infrastructure capex from hyperscalers continues to accelerate into 2027 with no signs of digestion.
ideas.key_risk: A hot CPI print Friday could compress high-multiple growth names sharply; US-Iran escalation could also disrupt Taiwanese semiconductor supply chains if the conflict expands regionally.

sources.label: Morgan Stanley Top Picks - TheStreet Pro

ideas.catalyst: WTI crude at $92.32 (+0.92% today) represents a ~29% spike from last week's ~$71.50 level — a massive fuel cost headwind that will materially compress airline margins in Q3 and Q4.
ideas.thesis: Jet fuel is approximately 20-25% of airline operating costs; a sustained WTI move from ~$71 to $92+ could erase $200-400M in quarterly earnings for Delta if the elevated price persists through September. With summer peak travel behind them, airlines have limited pricing power to offset this cost shock, and forward guidance revisions lower are likely when they next speak to the market.
ideas.key_risk: Rapid diplomatic resolution to the US-Iran conflict could collapse oil prices quickly; airlines may also have undisclosed hedge positions that limit downside margin exposure at current price levels.

ideas.catalyst: Macquarie raised Zscaler's price target from $172 to $200, maintaining Outperform; ongoing US-Iran war escalation historically accelerates enterprise zero-trust security spending as state-sponsored cyber threats rise alongside kinetic conflict.
ideas.thesis: Active nation-state cyber conflict correlates historically with accelerated enterprise cybersecurity spending, particularly for zero-trust architecture that defends against sophisticated state-sponsored intrusions. Zscaler's platform is the enterprise standard for cloud-native zero-trust, and the Macquarie PT lift signals improving revenue visibility — the geopolitical catalyst adds urgency to buying decisions at the CIO level.
ideas.key_risk: If the US-Iran conflict remains kinetic rather than transitioning to a cyber dimension, the security spending urgency may not materialize quickly in Q3 pipeline data; rising rates also compress ZS's high growth multiple.

ideas.catalyst: Goldman Sachs maintains UPS as a top conviction buy with $132 price target implying ~29% upside; stock yields 6.39%, one of the highest yields in Goldman's large-cap coverage universe.
ideas.thesis: UPS's 6.39% dividend yield provides a defensive income anchor in a volatile, rate-rising environment; at Goldman's $132 PT the risk-reward is compelling for income-oriented capital rotation out of rate-sensitive sectors. Global trade volumes running at 8.8% YoY growth support UPS's international network fundamentals and reduce downside risk to consensus estimates.
ideas.key_risk: Fuel cost spike from oil at $92 increases UPS's cost structure materially; energy surcharges may not fully offset the headwind if consumer shipping volumes soften alongside declining consumer sentiment (51.7 in August).

sources.label: Goldman Sachs Top Picks September 2026 - 24/7 Wall St.

ideas.catalyst: Macquarie raised Snowflake's price target from $200 to $350 — a $150 jump — while maintaining Neutral, signaling a dramatically improved fundamental view on the AI data cloud platform's trajectory.
ideas.thesis: The $150 Macquarie PT increase indicates that Snowflake's Cortex AI workloads and data-sharing platform are gaining enterprise traction materially ahead of prior expectations, likely driven by enterprises consolidating analytics workloads onto AI-native infrastructure. With the stock presumably trading well below the new $350 target, the upside to fair value creates a compelling medium-term opportunity as enterprise AI data management spend accelerates into year-end.
ideas.key_risk: Snowflake carries a premium valuation that compresses materially in a rising-rate environment; the Macquarie analyst maintained Neutral (not Outperform) suggesting near-term execution risk remains and the PT lift may reflect a longer-horizon view than swing traders can hold.

deals.headline: CRH Acquires Arcosa Inc. — Stockholder Approval Secured September 4
deals.description: Arcosa Inc. (ACA) stockholders voted to approve the acquisition by CRH, the global building materials giant, at a special meeting held on September 4, 2026. The deal is now on track for regulatory clearance and final close, adding Arcosa's construction products and engineered structures businesses to CRH's North American portfolio amid sustained IIJA-driven infrastructure spending.
deals.impact: Bullish for ACA as a takeout target trading close to deal price; CRH gains significant US infrastructure exposure with long-duration earnings visibility from the infrastructure construction supercycle.

deals.headline: SpaceX IPO Priced at $135/Share — Largest IPO on Record at ~$75B Valuation
deals.description: SpaceX completed its landmark IPO at $135 per share, implying a valuation of approximately $75 billion and making it the largest IPO on record globally. The debut represents a watershed moment for the commercial space industry and validates the dominant launch market position that SpaceX has built with Falcon 9 and the Starship development program.
deals.impact: Massive sentiment catalyst for the broader space economy and adjacent defense technology names; institutional capital that had been waiting to access SpaceX exposure will now have a liquid vehicle, potentially drawing funds from adjacent space and defense proxies.

deals.headline: Oura Health Files for Nasdaq IPO — Smart Ring Health Tracker Goes Public
deals.description: Oura Health, maker of the Oura Ring smart health-tracking wearable with over 3 million subscribers, announced plans to list on the Nasdaq exchange with its IPO filing emerging just ahead of the Labor Day holiday. The company competes in the rapidly growing continuous health monitoring market against Apple Watch and Garmin, with a differentiated ring form factor and proprietary health algorithms.
deals.impact: Bullish for wearables and digital health sector valuation; potential competitive pressure signal for Apple (AAPL) in premium wearables if Oura gains significant institutional visibility post-listing.

deals.headline: Anthropic IPO Targeted for Late September or October 2026
deals.description: Bloomberg reported that Anthropic, the AI safety company behind the Claude large language model platform, is targeting a public listing in late September or October 2026. The offering is expected to be among the most closely watched AI IPOs since the GPT-era acceleration, given Anthropic's position as the leading independent AI safety researcher and enterprise AI model provider competing with OpenAI.
deals.impact: A landmark AI IPO that will test institutional appetite for pure-play AI safety valuations; bullish sentiment catalyst for the AI sector broadly if priced well, though may siphon capital from listed AI proxies like NVDA, MSFT, GOOGL in the weeks surrounding the offering.

deals.headline: Nuvectis Pharma (NUVL) Enters 11-Day Binary Window to FDA Decision on Zidesamtinib
deals.description: With a PDUFA date of September 18, 2026 for zidesamtinib in ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer, Nuvectis Pharma enters the most consequential 11-day period in its corporate history. Management has pre-positioned for a commercial launch, disclosing commercial infrastructure preparations in recent filings, suggesting internal confidence in the outcome.
deals.impact: Binary event — FDA approval could re-rate the stock 2-5x while a Complete Response Letter could halve it; sophisticated biotech investors and options traders will be aggressively positioning around the Sept 18 PDUFA date in the days ahead.

key_events.headline: US-Iran War Escalation Drives WTI to $92.32 — Geopolitical Risk Premium at Cycle High
key_events.impact: Energy sector bull catalyst; airline and transport sector short pressure; safe-haven bid in dollar and gold; may accelerate Fed hawkish repricing if oil-driven CPI prints hot Friday.

key_events.impact: Thin global liquidity with European/Asian markets absorbing the weekend's US-Iran escalation news without US institutional participation; could amplify intraday volatility when US markets reopen Tuesday.

key_events.impact: A hawkish ECB hike to 2.75% would pressure European equities (especially rate-sensitive growth names) and emerging market assets that borrowed in euros; potential EUR/USD support on the rate differential.

key_events.impact: The week's defining macro event; with Fed hike odds at 57%, any print above 3.0% YoY cements the September rate hike and could trigger a broad risk-asset selloff with Treasury yields spiking.

key_events.impact: Dollar strength (DXY +0.27% to 99.09), Treasury price pressure, emerging market currency stress; REIT and utility names face multiple compression as terminal rate reprices higher.

key_events.impact: Positive demand signal for global semiconductor supply chain; bullish for NVDA, AMD, TSMC, Samsung, SK Hynix and their broader AI chip ecosystems heading into the US trading week.

risk_calendar.desc: Labor Day — US equity and bond markets closed. Asian and European markets open; US-Iran war escalation is the primary overnight driver.
ECB Rate Decision — Expected +25bp to 2.75%. A hawkish surprise above consensus would pressure European equities and EM assets broadly.
US CPI (August) — Before the bell. Consensus ~2.8% YoY. A hot print above 3% cements the September Fed rate hike and triggers broad risk-asset repricing.
Kroger (KR) fiscal Q2 2026 earnings — Consensus EPS $1.06 on $34.61B revenue. Key consumer health read ahead of the holiday shopping season.
Zidesamtinib (NUVL) FDA decision for ROS1+ non-small cell lung cancer — binary biotech catalyst with approval or CRL outcome.
OST-HER2 (OSTX) BLA review for osteosarcoma and apitegromab (SRRK) for spinal muscular atrophy — dual binary biotech events at month-end.

runs.market_commentary:
Asian markets closed the week strongly with the Nikkei 225 posting a 1.26% gain on Friday, closing at 65,021 — its highest level in over a month — driven by easing rate-hike concerns from the Bank of Japan and continued enthusiasm around Japanese semiconductor and robotics exporters benefiting from South Korea's semiconductor export boom (exports tripled year-over-year). Broader Asia sentiment was supported by a pickup in global trade volumes, which rose 8.8% YoY and 3.3% month-over-month in June, the second-fastest monthly gain since 2023.

European markets closed modestly higher on Friday, with the DAX at 21,847 (+0.38%) and FTSE at 8,718 (+0.22%), though gains were capped by a troubling inflation reading: Euro zone CPI climbed back above 3%, prompting renewed speculation about additional ECB rate action. The AI data center construction boom was flagged by Bloomberg as insufficient to offset a broader US and European construction sector slump, pressuring rate-sensitive real estate and utilities stocks.

US markets are closed Monday September 7 for Labor Day, making this a four-day trading week. Last Friday saw mixed pre-market futures — Dow futures slipped ~10 pts (-0.02%), S&P 500 futures -0.06%, and Nasdaq-100 futures -0.10% — but sentiment firmed intraday following Trump comments that 'market will go up,' per Benzinga. The key macro focus for the week is the August inflation print: PPI drops Thursday before the bell and CPI drops Friday before the bell. Any CPI surprise above 3% would reprice Fed rate-cut odds materially. Kroger reports fiscal Q2 earnings Friday as well, providing a consumer health read.

ideas.catalyst: Morgan Stanley maintains NVDA as its core AI play heading into a week where AI data center demand commentary is expected from multiple tech conferences.
ideas.thesis: NVIDIA's data center GPU franchise continues to benefit from hyperscaler capex acceleration, with South Korea semiconductor export data (tripled YoY) confirming robust end-demand across the supply chain. The stock has institutional tailwinds entering the holiday-shortened week with no adverse earnings risk until late Q3.
ideas.key_risk: Any CPI upside surprise Friday could reprice risk assets broadly, pressuring high-multiple tech names including NVDA.

ideas.catalyst: Macquarie raised Snowflake's price target from $200 to $350 this week, maintaining Neutral — a massive $150 PT jump signals significantly improved fundamental view on the data cloud platform.
ideas.thesis: The sharp Macquarie PT increase to $350 suggests Snowflake's AI-native data platform is gaining enterprise traction faster than consensus expects, likely driven by its Cortex AI workloads. With the stock trading well below the new target, the setup favors upside into the next earnings cycle.
ideas.key_risk: Rising rates from a hot CPI print would hurt growth multiples; Snowflake carries a premium valuation that compresses in risk-off environments.

ideas.catalyst: FDA PDUFA date for zidesamtinib (ROS1+ non-small cell lung cancer) is September 18, 2026 — 12 days away.
ideas.thesis: Zidesamtinib targets a validated oncology niche with significant unmet need; ROS1+ NSCLC patients have limited approved options and ROS1 inhibitors have shown strong clinical profiles in this indication. A positive FDA decision on Sept 18 would be a transformative binary catalyst for this small-cap biotech.
ideas.key_risk: Binary FDA risk — a Complete Response Letter or label restriction would send the stock sharply lower; position sizing accordingly.

sources.label: Biotech Stocks Facing FDA Decision Sept 2026 - RTTNews

ideas.catalyst: Apitegromab has a FDA PDUFA date of September 30, 2026 for the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA).
ideas.thesis: SMA is a high-value rare disease market; apitegromab targets a mechanism complementary to existing SMA treatments (Spinraza, Zolgensma) and could carve out significant market share if approved. Scholar Rock's recent 8-K filings suggest the company is positioning for a commercial launch.
ideas.key_risk: FDA may request additional data given the complexity of SMA combination therapy; approval is not guaranteed and timeline could slip to 2027.

ideas.catalyst: Goldman Sachs maintains UPS as a top pick with a $132 price target implying ~29% upside; stock yields 6.39%, one of the highest in Goldman's coverage universe.
ideas.thesis: Global trade volumes surged 8.8% YoY in June, the second-fastest monthly growth since 2023, directly benefiting UPS's international and domestic package networks. At a 6.39% dividend yield with Goldman's $132 PT, the risk-reward skews favorably for income-oriented investors.
ideas.key_risk: Any deterioration in consumer spending or a trade-war escalation could dampen package volume growth and pressure the dividend if cash flows weaken.

Kiplinger Economic Data Week of Sept 7-11

ideas.catalyst: Morgan Stanley names Amazon as a top pick alongside NVDA for the AI infrastructure supercycle, with AWS continuing to take cloud market share.
ideas.thesis: Amazon's tripartite exposure to AI (AWS Bedrock, custom Trainium chips, Alexa+) creates compounding optionality across cloud, consumer AI, and advertising. AWS re-acceleration is the key near-term driver and management commentary at upcoming conferences should serve as a positive catalyst.
ideas.key_risk: Antitrust scrutiny remains a tail risk; any regulatory action against AWS or the retail marketplace could overhang the stock.

Goldman Sachs & Morgan Stanley Picks Sept 2026 - CNBC

ideas.catalyst: Macquarie raised Zscaler's price target from $172 to $200, maintaining Outperform, reflecting confidence in the zero-trust security platform's enterprise penetration.
ideas.thesis: Zero-trust architecture continues to be a board-level priority across enterprises as hybrid work and AI tool proliferation expand attack surfaces. Zscaler's platform-based approach is outpacing point-product competitors, and the Macquarie PT lift suggests improving visibility into the next few quarters.
ideas.key_risk: Cybersecurity spending can be discretionary; any macro slowdown signaled by this week's CPI print could cause CIOs to delay purchasing decisions.

ideas.catalyst: Wells Fargo raised Amgen's price target from $400 to $435, maintaining Equal-Weight — a constructive PT lift suggesting improved pipeline or revenue visibility.
ideas.thesis: Amgen's obesity pipeline (MariTide) and inflammation franchise (Repatha, Otezla) provide durable growth drivers while the stock's relative defensive characteristics offer portfolio ballast heading into a potential CPI shock this Friday. The $435 Wells Fargo PT implies meaningful upside from current levels.
ideas.key_risk: Pipeline setbacks in obesity (any MariTide trial data miss) or biosimilar competition to legacy products could weigh on the stock.

ideas.catalyst: UBS raised Teva's price target to $48 with a Buy rating, reflecting improved confidence in the generic pharma giant's debt reduction and pipeline progression.
ideas.thesis: Teva is executing on a multi-year turnaround anchored by opioid settlement resolution, biosimilar launches, and the growing AUSTEDO franchise for tardive dyskinesia and Huntington's chorea. At UBS's $48 target, Teva trades at a significant discount to specialty pharma peers, offering a valuation re-rating opportunity.
ideas.key_risk: Teva carries significant debt; rising interest rates from a hot inflation print could pressure refinancing economics and delay deleveraging targets.

ideas.catalyst: Kroger reports fiscal Q2 2026 earnings Friday September 11, with consensus expecting EPS of $1.06 on revenue of $34.61 billion — a potential beat given grocery inflation dynamics.
ideas.thesis: Food-at-home inflation has stayed sticky above general CPI, benefiting Kroger's private label and loyalty program economics. If Thursday's PPI and Friday's CPI show continued services inflation, Kroger's grocery pricing power narrative strengthens as consumers trade down from restaurants.
ideas.key_risk: Post-merger integration costs (from the Albertsons saga) and competitive pressure from Walmart and Amazon Fresh could disappoint on margins versus the EPS consensus.

deals.headline: Eli Lilly Acquires Merida Biosciences for Autoimmune Pipeline
deals.description: Eli Lilly announced an agreement to acquire Merida Biosciences, a privately-held biotech developing a new class of precision therapeutics for serious autoimmune and allergic diseases, on September 1, 2026. The deal underscores Lilly's strategy to diversify beyond its blockbuster GLP-1 weight-loss franchise into high-value immunology.
deals.impact: Bullish for LLY – adds pipeline optionality in a fast-growing immune-mediated disease market without dilutive equity issuance.

deals.headline: EQT Pays $2B for Majority Stake in McGill and Partners
deals.description: EQT, the Swedish private equity giant, announced plans on September 4, 2026 to pay $2 billion for a majority stake in McGill and Partners, a specialty (re)insurance broker. The deal reflects continued PE appetite for fee-generating insurance distribution assets, which carry lower catastrophe risk than underwriters.
deals.impact: Moderately bullish for EQT shares as the deal signals disciplined capital deployment into high-quality insurance distribution at a time of robust commercial lines pricing.

deals.headline: SHEIN Lists on Hong Kong Stock Exchange in Landmark Fast-Fashion IPO
deals.description: SHEIN completed its listing on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on September 1, 2026, in one of the year's most anticipated retail IPOs. The Chinese-founded fast-fashion giant had faced multiple delays and regulatory hurdles across US and UK listing attempts before pivoting to Hong Kong.
deals.impact: Competitive pressure signal for Western fast-fashion and e-commerce players; capital markets constructive on Hong Kong bourse's ability to attract major listings.

deals.headline: FDA Grants Accelerated Approval for TUDRIQEV in Advanced Melanoma
deals.description: On August 6, 2026, the FDA granted accelerated approval for TUDRIQEV (vusolimogene oderparepvec-wtpg) for adult patients with unresectable advanced cutaneous melanoma who experienced disease progression on an anti-PD-1 antibody. The approval opens a new commercial opportunity in the competitive checkpoint inhibitor-refractory melanoma market.
deals.impact: Positive regulatory precedent for oncolytic virotherapy; bullish signal for other companies in the immuno-oncology and oncolytic virus space ahead of September FDA calendar.

deals.headline: Anthropic IPO Expected Late September / October 2026
deals.description: Bloomberg reported on August 24, 2026, that Anthropic, the AI safety company and maker of Claude, is anticipated to pursue an IPO in late September or October 2026. Separately, OURA Health (the smart ring maker) may also IPO as early as September, per the same report.
deals.impact: Potential landmark AI IPO would be a sentiment catalyst for AI infrastructure and software names; could siphon capital from listed AI proxies like NVDA, MSFT, GOOGL if institutional reallocation occurs.

key_events.impact: The week's defining data point; consensus expects ~2.8% YoY. Any print above 3% would materially reprice Fed rate-cut expectations for 2026.

key_events.impact: Higher ECB terminal rate expectations pressure European bond markets and reduce equity multiple expansion for European stocks.

key_events.impact: Strong validation of AI chip demand cycle; bullish for memory and logic semiconductor names globally (Samsung, SK Hynix, TSMC, NVDA, AMD).

key_events.headline: Kroger Fiscal Q2 2026 Earnings — Friday September 11
key_events.impact: Consensus: EPS $1.06 on revenue $34.61B. A beat would confirm grocery pricing power; a miss on margins would weigh on consumer staples broadly.
